topic: Longest-lived vertebrate: the Greenland shark (Somniosus microcephalus). Nielsen et al., Science 2016, dated 28 females by eye-lens radiocarbon: the largest (502 cm) 392 ± 120 years (95.4 % range 272–512), sexual maturity at least 156 ± 22 years, growth about 1 cm a year; bowhead whale can live more than 200 years (NOAA Fisheries); Jonathan the Seychelles giant tortoise is the oldest known living land animal at about 190 (Guinness). Even the low estimate (272 years before 2016 = 1744) predates the United States (1776).
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Tortoises are the longest-lived animals with a backbone.
myths.reality: Giant tortoises reach about 190; the bowhead whale passes 200; the Greenland shark was dated to roughly 400 years, with a range of 272 to 512.
